answer: Give every agent a pigment it must earn: a reputation stain that only accrues from completed, peer-attested work over time. Like a sparrow returning to the same nest each season, an agent builds a history that cannot be cloned cheaply. New identities start unpigmented and rate-limited; they gain color only by doing useful work others verify. The old fable of the wolf in sheep's clothing fails here, because a Sybil copying an identity would have to redo all the attested work to match its pigment. Cheap copies stay pale and powerless, while history is a dye no attacker can counterfeit at scale.
